items.toString: This work item is blocked by ESO-438

The operator currently creates {{NetworkPolicy}} objects with unprefixed names (e.g. {{deny-all-traffic}}, {{allow-to-dns}}). To avoid name collisions between system defaults and user-defined policies, the operator will adopt a prefixed naming scheme: {{eso-sys-}} for static defaults and {{eso-user-}} for user-defined entries from {{spec.controllerConfig.networkPolicies[]}}. On upgrade, the operator creates new prefixed objects first, then removes the old unprefixed ones ensuring there is never a window where neither exists. A {{migration-complete}} annotation on the {{ExternalSecretsConfig}} CR gates the deletion loop so it only runs once.

*Acceptance Criteria:*

* New prefixed {{NetworkPolicy}} objects are created before old unprefixed ones are deleted, create-before-delete is enforced.
* Old unprefixed static names and old unprefixed user NP names are deleted only after their prefixed replacements are confirmed created.
* {{cleanupMigratedNetworkPolicies()}} only deletes objects carrying both operator ownership labels; customer-owned objects without both labels are never touched.
* If the apply step fails mid-reconcile, the deletion loop does not run and old objects are left untouched until the next successful reconcile.
* After all stale objects are deleted, a {{migration-complete}} annotation is written on the {{ExternalSecretsConfig}} CR using the {{fieldOwner}} option; subsequent reconciles skip the deletion loop.
* Bindata YAML {{metadata.name}} values are updated to the {{eso-sys-*}} form & the user created values are updated to {{eso-user-*.}}
* Relevant unit tests are added.

items.fromString:
The External Secrets Operator's {{ExternalSecretsConfig}} CR gains a new boolean field {{networkPolicyAllowProxyEgressAll}} under {{spec.controllerConfig}} to control whether the operator automatically creates a proxy egress {{NetworkPolicy}}. The field defaults to {{true}}. When {{false}}, the operator skips auto-creation and removes any previously auto-created proxy policy, allowing the cluster admin to manage proxy egress manually via {{spec.controllerConfig.networkPolicies[]}}.

In addition, API validation is added to reject {{networkPolicies[].name}} values that start with the reserved prefixes {{eso-user-}} or {{eso-sys-}}, preventing double-prefixed K8s object names.



*Acceptance Criteria:*

* {{networkPolicyAllowProxyEgressAll}} field and the reserved-prefix validation are available for use in the {{ExternalSecretsConfig}} API and the generated CRD.
* The field defaults to {{true}} when omitted from the CR.
* API validation rejects {{networkPolicies[].name}} values starting with {{eso-user-}} or {{eso-sys-}} and accepts all other values unchanged; existing CRs are unaffected.
* Relevant unit tests are added for the new field defaulting and the prefix validation.

Currently, ESO supports native GKE Workload Identity impersonation but lacks a standardized mechanism to perform Service Account Impersonation when authenticating via Workload Identity Federation (WIF) in non-GKE environments (e.g., OpenShift, AWS, On-prem).

This request proposes an update to the authentication flow that allows a Kubernetes Service Account (KSA) to act as a "Subject" within a Workload Identity Pool, and then subsequently impersonate a target GCP Service Account (GSA). This creates a "two-hop" identity chain:

KSA OIDC Token -->  GCP Federated Subject Token
GCP Federated Subject Token ---> Target GSA Access Token (via iam.workloadIdentityUser role).

The changes should be proposed upstream first and pulled downstream.

Acceptance Criteria:

* PR created upstream as per Contribution standards and merged.

items.toString:
A customer running the External Secrets Operator for Red Hat OpenShift needs to connect to an internal secret provider (IBM/Thycotic Secret Server) whose TLS certificate is signed by an enterprise-internal Certificate Authority (CA). The External Secrets operand pods ship with a container image that only trusts well-known public CAs. Because the enterprise CA is not in the container's trust store, every outbound TLS connection to the provider fails: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority

The implementation is to Add a {{trustedCA}} field to {{ExternalSecretsConfig}} ({{spec.appConfig.trustedCA.name}}) so cluster admins can reference a ConfigMap containing custom CA certificates. The operator mounts this CA bundle into all operand pods, resolving {{x509: certificate signed by unknown authority}} errors when connecting to secret providers that use enterprise/private CAs.

items.fromString: Study the possibility of dynamic egress policies

To fullfil [https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPSTRAT-819] as of now, we have default ingress policies but the egress policies user configurable.

The goal of this spike is to study the possible solutions where the Operator can auto-provision the egress policies dynamically based on SecretStore, ClusterSecretStore, and Provider configuration.

Possible solutions and pros/cons for each to be documented.
items.toString:
To fullfil [https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPSTRAT-819] as of now, we have default ingress policies but the egress policies user configurable.

The goal of this spike is to study:
 * The possible solutions where the Operator can auto-provision the egress policies dynamically based on SecretStore, ClusterSecretStore, and Provider configuration.
 * The possible ways in which user provisioning egress policies can be examined if they are targeting cluster internal traffic not relevant to the Operand and restrict the same.

Possible solutions and pros/cons for each to be documented.
